verdict: When I Work: Choose When I Work when cheap per-user hourly scheduling is the job — not when clocks must be in the headline price, or when you need restaurant-only or hub-style WFM. Scores use the HR editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
weaknesses: Time & attendance not in the $2.50 headline
AI is not a product pillar
bestFor: Hourly teams that mainly need scheduling and messaging at a low per-user price
Operators who will trial 14 days before buying Deputy or Homebase hubs
Multi-location teams that stay on Essentials+ for templates and OpenShifts
notIdealFor: Teams whose primary job is GPS time clocks (Jibble) without paying the T&A toggle
Restaurants that want 7shifts’ hospitality payroll/tips stack
Buyers who need a free forever WFM tier (Homebase Basic / Connecteam ≤10)
tradeoffs: Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs
Hub / multi-module pricing complexity vs single-product floors
Mobile/frontline readiness vs desk-bound admin depth
Opaque contact-sales pricing vs transparent published seats
recommendation: Choose When I Work when cheap per-user hourly scheduling is the job — not when clocks must be in the headline price, or when you need restaurant-only or hub-style WFM. Compare Homebase for a free tiny-team tier, Connecteam for deskless hubs, Deputy for compliance-heavy shift work, and 7shifts for restaurants.
editorialNotes: HR Priority-2 batch. Approved on hr-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=frontline-wfm. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Long-standing simple hourly scheduler with a 14-day trial. Score is research-grounded, not lab-tested.
Primary job is frontline scheduling/comms. Fit is strong for that cluster; T&A is add-on so not a time-clock specialist.
OpenShifts, templates, and auto-scheduling on Essentials+ are solid. Premium unlocks API/SSO.
POS/payroll connectors including a Rippling partnership are adequate for hourly stacks.
Mobile-first scheduling and messaging are the product thesis.
Forecasting/reporting deepen on Pro; not Deputy-class analytics add-ons.
Per-user path plus Enterprise contact supports growth; T&A packaging is the main ops friction.
Low $2.50 scheduling floor is strong if you do not need clocks; clocks raise real TCO. Affiliate economics excluded.
Auto-scheduler/forecasting are marketed; no named AI suite like Deputy AI — scored limited.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine HR editorial criteria using the category weights (hiring/workforce fit 15, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, value 12, mobile/frontline 10, scalability 9, analytics 8, AI 8), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ATS, core HRIS, payroll/benefits, people-platform, frontline WFM, time & attendance, SOP training, and LMS peers are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
